title: Love Bullet
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Koharu Sakurada, a fifteen-year-old matchmaker with no romantic experience, is killed saving her best friend Aki from a falling pole just as she is about to confess her love. The Goddess of Love lets her return as a Cupid, an immortal winged agent who matches couples with guns instead of arrows and earns karma toward a return to life. Her first job is to help the grieving Aki fall for someone new, and rival Cupids soon turn missions into shoot-outs.
life_message: Love means wanting the other person's happiness, even when it is not with you.

content.note: Koharu is impaled saving Aki; Cupids fight with guns, sniper rifles and bombs, played largely for action-comedy (Wikipedia; AniList Guns 86).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Cupid rivalries flare into shoot-outs but are settled by cooperation, not honor feuds.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Cupids work from a central board with rules but roam freely and bend them.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friendship with Aki matters more than family; Cupids serve whoever is posted.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Mentor Kanna and the Goddess have authority; Cupids are rough equals.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Spiritual afterlife run like a modern job with operating costs.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Earning karma to live again versus helping love flourish.

folkways.japan: The karma economy and matchmaking as 'en-musubi' (tying bonds) echo Japanese Buddhist and Shinto ideas, mixed with Western Cupid imagery.

winners_losers: Aki finds new love and Koharu grows by letting go; possessive love loses. Sympathy goes to selfless love.
